key_insight: An AI-assisted workflow for tissue-based antibody interpretation improved accuracy, especially for novice readers, compared with unaided interpretation.
clinical_relevance: This could help standardize autoimmune encephalitis autoantibody screening and reduce reader-dependent variability in centralized laboratory workflows.
method: Trained an interpretable deep-learning model on 2,357 retrospective serum and CSF tissue-based assay images from >80 institutions.
Prospectively validated the system on 200 new images from 200 unique patients using expert-consensus labels.
Compared two experts and two novices reading the same cases unaided versus with AI assistance after a washout period.
evidence_signal: In prospective validation, the standalone classifier achieved AUROC 0.922 and the AI-assisted reader round raised pooled accuracy from 90.4% to 97.4% (McNemar P < 0.001).
watch_item: Results come from a centralized, prospective validation setting, so multicenter cross-platform performance and real-world workflow robustness still need confirmation.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study
